data-icon-only.when: the button shows only an icon; aria-label then carries its name

root.note: a when it has an href, button otherwise.

elements.when: the site supplies an arrow and the button is a section's call to action: the hero's, the call-to-action section's and a media-text row's buttons (in salt-hero__actions, salt-cta__actions, salt-media-text__actions), a process step's action and the collection showcase's view-all link
elements.note: Text and arrow together, so the arrow wraps with the last word. Exactly the buttons the condition names take the site's arrow, as Salt for Next.js draws them. Never: the pricing plan's action, the header's call to action, the case study view's live link, the service view's call to action, the contact form's submit, the map's load button.

zeroState: Not drawn without a label, or, in link form, without a resolvable href.

hooks.reason: Groups the text and its arrow; the word joiner inside the arrow keeps them on one line. No rule needed, but sites and tests target the label.

notes.text: WordPress's link-arrow style is the link style plus the arrow component; its size argument goes (one size, floored by section#target-size).

formerly.note: span[aria-hidden] with a right arrow entity, inside x-button-link-arrow

owes: Style as data-style, not a class per style; add data-track-control='cta'; draw the arrow through the arrow component inside span.salt-button__label.

The site's arrow in span.salt-button__label on exactly the buttons the label's condition names (the hero, call-to-action and media-text buttons, a step's action, the showcase's view-all link), and on no other button.
